text:
Ivar Stenberg is 19, a month into his NHL career after going second overall in June, and The Hockey Writers already call him the one thing going right for the Sharks. He scored in regulation and then won the eight-round shootout against the Islanders on Nov. 9 to end a five-game skid, his third goal in four games. Twelve points in 20 games (six goals) is right on the median for forwards picked first to fourth: those players averaged 0.56 points a game in their first full seasons, and he's at 0.60.

Eight of his 12 points have come on the power play, where he's on the top unit with Celebrini and Smith, and that's the engine of his scoring. At five on five the Sharks have been buried with him out there (40% of the expected goals), though they've also scored 4.1 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. His shooting percentage (19.4%) will cool, but he's creating his own chances at a good clip. He came from Frölunda, where he had 33 points in 43 SHL games. Our middle projection: about 20 goals and 49 points.
